issues: passes Ito gate only via ATAC 0.163 (in-sample threshold)
cell_type unlabeled in results.csv (actually primary human CD8+ T cells)
rationale: Direction is right and the guide passes the full Ito rule, but a single guide cannot distinguish a working score from luck, and the score materially underpredicts the observed 91% indel. No off-target assessment exists for this or any other guide.

issues: ATAC (0.438, 0.519) is non-discriminating here - both guides high
Ito thresholds fit and tested on this same 205-guide set
rationale: Both guides show high sequence scores and high measured indel (93%, 85%), so the ranking signal is internally consistent. Confidence is capped below 0.7 because accessibility contributes nothing separable here and off-target risk is entirely unassessed.

issues: DeepSpCas9 19.5 guide outperforms the DeepSpCas9 42.1 guide
rank inversion between the gene's two guides
rationale: The score ranks the two BACH2 guides in the wrong order - the guide with much worse DeepSpCas9 (19.5 vs 42.1) and worse CHOPCHOP (0.07 vs 0.17) achieved higher indel (53.5% vs 39.5%). This is a direct local failure of the ranking value the metric recommends.

issues: no negative control guide for this gene
rationale: A single concordant guide (seq 0.63, ATAC 0.806, 70% indel) passing the Ito rule. Consistent but unreplicated, and it contributes nothing to distinguishing the sequence term from the accessibility term.

issues: identical ATAC (0.062) for guides with 88.75% and 0.0% indel
worst-scoring guide by DeepSpCas9 (29.2) had the highest indel (88.75%)
accessibility term has zero discriminating power at this locus
0.0% indel may be assay failure, not biology
rationale: Two guides share the same ATAC signal but span the entire outcome range (0% to 88.75%), so accessibility cannot explain anything here, and the sequence term ranks them backwards. This gene is a clean counterexample to both scored components.

issues: high ATAC (0.62, 0.604) guides gave 1.5% and 0.0% indel
two of three guides are near-zero outcomes
rationale: All three guides sit in open chromatin (ATAC 0.60-0.81) yet two produced essentially no editing, so the accessibility term is uninformative-to-misleading here. Only the sequence score separates the working guide, and it does so weakly.

issues: 81% indel at ATAC 0.0155 (~2 read counts, lowest bin)
gene name also appears as 'CDKN2C ' with trailing whitespace - split record
rationale: The best-performing guide (81% indel) has the lowest ATAC signal in the gene, directly inverting the accessibility premise. Gene-level aggregation is additionally corrupted by a trailing-whitespace duplicate key in results.csv.

issues: data hygiene bug - trailing whitespace creates a phantom gene
any per-gene aggregation downstream is silently wrong
rationale: This is not a real gene entry; it is CDKN2C with a trailing space that Agent 4 never normalized. Its existence means gene-level grouping, ranking, and any Agent 6/7 aggregation over this table is quietly incorrect.

issues: highest CHOPCHOP guide (0.93) gave only 15% indel
both components rank the 4 guides poorly
rationale: Neither component orders CTBP1's four guides correctly: the most accessible guide failed completely and the highest CHOPCHOP guide underperformed badly. Only the DeepSpCas9=12.7 guide is correctly predicted to fail.

issues: both guides scored low (seq 0.38, 0.19) but achieved ~55% indel
rationale: Both guides are predicted poor by sequence and accessibility yet both edited at ~55-56%. If used prospectively the metric would have discarded two usable guides at this locus.

issues: passes Ito gate but only 57% indel (near the 50% efficiency boundary)
ATAC 1.29 is far above threshold yet outcome is mid-range
rationale: Concordant in sign but weak in magnitude - a guide in highly open chromatin with good sequence scores returned only a mid-range 57% indel. Single-guide evidence with no replication.

issues: rank inversion: seq 0.30 guide -> 0% indel, seq 0.21 guide -> 66.5% indel
both guides low ATAC, opposite outcomes
rationale: The metric orders the two guides backwards and both accessibility values are low despite one guide editing at 66.5%. No component provides usable signal at this locus.

issues: DNMT3A is one of Ito's 5 PROSPECTIVE validation genes - these are the training-set guides, not the validated ones
confirms results.csv is Ito's discovery set, not a held-out set
no positive example to test ranking against
rationale: The score correctly predicts failure for all three guides, but this gene exposes a structural problem: Ito's successful DNMT3A guides came from their prospective design round and are absent from this table, so Agent 4 benchmarked only the discovery set from which the thresholds were derived.

issues: highest indel guide (75%) has lowest DeepSpCas9 (53.9) of the three
ATAC essentially constant (0.031-0.054) across a 0-75% outcome range
rationale: Outcomes span 0-75% while ATAC varies only between 0.031 and 0.054, so accessibility cannot separate them, and the sequence term ranks the best guide last. Low trust in any DOT1L recommendation.

issues: accessibility inverted: ATAC 0.0697 -> 87% indel, ATAC 0.697 -> 47.5% indel
10x ATAC difference in the wrong direction
rationale: The two guides differ tenfold in accessibility and the less accessible one edited nearly twice as well. Sequence score gets the ordering right, which is the only reason this is not scored lower.

issues: both guides 0% indel despite ATAC above threshold (0.116, 0.093)
possible amplicon/assay failure rather than true inefficiency
no positive example at this locus
rationale: Both guides sit at or near the ATAC>=0.1 cutoff yet produced zero editing, which the accessibility term cannot explain. Uniform zeros also raise the possibility of a locus-level assay failure that the score does not model.

issues: both guides edited well (84%, 75%) despite 16x ATAC difference (0.492 vs 0.031)
rationale: Both guides work, so a user would not be harmed, but the accessibility term would have wrongly deprioritized the ATAC=0.031 guide that still achieved 75% indel. The components disagree with each other and with the outcome ordering.

issues: all 5 guides failed (1.0-17.5% indel) despite strong sequence scores
one guide passes ATAC>=0.1 and still failed
strong locus-level confounder not modeled by any component
rationale: This is the clearest evidence of an unmodeled gene-level confounder: the single best-scoring guide in the entire DUSP22 set (DeepSpCas9 80.7, CHOPCHOP 0.97) produced 1% indel, and all five guides failed. Something locus-specific - copy number, amplicon design, or essentiality - dominates, and the score has no term for it.

issues: highest DeepSpCas9 guide (68.3) at lowest ATAC (0.0155) gave 45.5% indel
lowest DeepSpCas9 guide (30.7) gave the highest indel (54%)
rank inversion across all three guides
rationale: The sequence term orders EHMT1's three guides almost exactly backwards relative to measured indel. Accessibility adds nothing, spanning only 0.0155-0.116.

issues: highest indel guide (55%) has CHOPCHOP 0.04 - near the bottom of the scale
ATAC 0.108 (passes cutoff) vs 0.0697 gives no useful separation
rationale: The best guide by measured indel scores worst on CHOPCHOP, so the recommended ranking value fails at this locus. Accessibility values cluster too tightly to discriminate.

issues: all 5 guides below ATAC threshold - accessibility term contributes no ranking information
best guide (40.5% indel) has the lowest ATAC (0.031)
rationale: Every FHL2 guide is in closed chromatin by Ito's cutoff, so accessibility is a constant and cannot rank anything; within that set it is inverted. Sequence ordering is only loosely correct and no guide reaches the 50% efficiency bar.

issues: ATAC constant-low (0.0155-0.031) across a 2.5-64.5% outcome range
DeepSpCas9 25.7 guide gave 59% indel; DeepSpCas9 50.4 guide gave 2.5%
rationale: Accessibility is effectively constant across four guides whose outcomes span 2.5% to 64.5%, and the sequence term inverts the top and bottom guides. Neither scored component is usable at this locus.

issues: accessibility strongly anti-correlated: ATAC 0.523 -> 3.5% indel, ATAC 0.0542 -> 47% indel
4 guides, accessibility uninformative or inverted in 3
rationale: FOXO1 is a direct counterexample to the accessibility premise: the most open guide edited worst (3.5%) and a nearly closed guide edited at 47%. The combined score's ATAC weight actively degrades the ranking here.

issues: 95.5% indel - among the highest in the dataset - at ATAC 0.0232 (near-lowest bin)
would be rejected by the Ito accessibility gate
rationale: The single FOXO3 guide achieved 95.5% editing while sitting in essentially closed chromatin, meaning the accessibility gate would have discarded one of the best guides in the entire benchmark. Strong single-point evidence against the ATAC filter.

issues: correct ordering but one guide at 0% indel
accessibility separates the working guide only weakly (0.147 vs 0.0697/0.0852)
rationale: The score ranks the three FURIN guides in the correct order and the top guide edited at 84.75%. Confidence is limited by a complete-failure guide whose cause is unmodeled and by unassessed off-target risk.

issues: passes the full Ito rule (DeepSpCas9 79.0, CHOPCHOP 0.72, ATAC 0.132) but only 36% indel
false positive of the high-precision gate
rationale: This guide satisfies every threshold in Ito's validated rule and still fell well short of the 50% efficiency definition. It is one of the 4 false positives that produce the gate's 0.862 precision, and with n=1 there is no way to tell whether GATA6 is systematically hard.

issues: CHOPCHOP 0.72 and DeepSpCas9 55.7 yet only 7% indel
rationale: A guide with a good CHOPCHOP score returned 7% editing, a large overprediction by the recommended ranking value. Single-guide evidence with no way to attribute the failure.
Both scored components would have rejected a guide that edited at 56.5%. This is a false-negative that the high-precision/low-recall gate is structurally prone to produce.
The score correctly identifies a poor guide, but correctly predicting failure is the easier half of the problem and one guide provides no evidence about ranking among usable candidates.

issues: ATAC 0.116 is only ~2 read counts above the 0.1 cutoff
rationale: Strong concordance - sequence_efficacy 0.824 and DeepSpCas9 75.9 predicting 84% measured indel, passing the full rule. Unreplicated, and its gate pass rests on an ATAC value barely above a noise-sensitive threshold.

issues: both guides edited well (82%, 79%) but neither passes the Ito gate
gate would reject two good guides
rationale: Both guides work well, so the outcome is favorable, but the CHOPCHOP>=0.3 condition would have rejected the better of the two. Evidence that the gate's recall problem has real cost.

issues: ATAC 1.75 gave 73.5% indel - same locus, both wide open
accessibility has no explanatory power at maximal openness
rationale: Both ID2 guides are in extremely open chromatin yet one edited at 73.5% and the other not at all, so accessibility saturates and stops carrying information exactly where the score treats it as maximally favorable. The min(1, atac/0.1) normalization makes these two guides indistinguishable on that term.

issues: accessibility inverted at the top of the range
rationale: The sequence term is roughly directionally correct across five guides but accessibility is inverted between the two best performers. No KDM1A guide clears the 50% bar convincingly, so all recommendations here are marginal.

issues: best guide (93.5% indel) FAILS the gate on ATAC 0.0968 vs 0.1 cutoff - a ~1 read-count margin
87% indel guide has DeepSpCas9 39.7 (would be rejected)
9 guides give the best within-gene evidence in the dataset
rationale: With 9 guides KEAP1 shows the sequence term working in aggregate, but it also contains the single most damaging threshold artifact in the benchmark: the top guide at 93.5% indel is rejected because its ATAC is 0.0968 rather than 0.1, a difference of roughly one sequencing read. The cutoff is being applied at a precision the measurement does not support.

issues: three of six gave 0-0.5% indel despite maximal accessibility
accessibility term is maximally wrong at this locus
rationale: KLF2 is the strongest counterexample to the project's central premise in the entire dataset: every guide sits in highly accessible chromatin, the accessibility term saturates at 1.0 for all six, and half of them produced essentially no editing. Any score that weights accessibility positively will confidently recommend guides that do not work here.

issues: no failing guide at this locus for contrast
rationale: Excellent concordance: sequence_efficacy 0.832, DeepSpCas9 76.4, CHOPCHOP 0.90, ATAC 0.364, measured 89% indel, passing every threshold comfortably. Unreplicated and off-target-unassessed, which caps confidence.

issues: both guides edited well (70%, 66%) but neither passes the Ito gate
better-performing guide has the LOWER DeepSpCas9 (43.7 vs 58.9)
rationale: Both guides are usable but the sequence term orders them backwards and the gate would reject both. Outcome-favorable, ranking-unfavorable.

issues: best guide (74.75% indel) correctly top-ranked by sequence score
but its ATAC 0.0658 would fail the gate
one guide at 0% indel with mid-range scores
rationale: The sequence term correctly identifies the best of four MTA2 guides, which is the behavior the metric claims. The accessibility gate would nonetheless discard that guide, again showing the two components pulling in opposite directions.
One guide with an unremarkable score that failed almost completely. Too little information to judge the metric, and the failure is unexplained by any component.

issues: the only guide passing the full Ito rule gave 5% indel - a gate false positive
PRDM1 is one of Ito's prospective validation genes; these training-set guides behave oppositely
rationale: The guide the metric most confidently recommends (passes all three thresholds) is the worst performer at 5% indel, while the guide with the lowest DeepSpCas9 score edited at 52%. Ito reported their prospectively designed PRDM1 guides all worked, which underscores that this table is the discovery set and its apparent gate performance is not out-of-sample.

issues: ATAC 6.32 - the highest in the entire dataset - gave 1% indel
rationale: The most accessible target site in the whole benchmark produced 1% editing. Combined with KLF2 and ID2, this shows the accessibility term's failures are concentrated precisely at high ATAC values where the score is most confident.

issues: 10 guides, mostly high indel at LOW ATAC (0.0155-0.0697)
only 1 of 10 passes the Ito gate; 8 guides above 60% indel would be rejected
accessibility gate would discard 92.5%, 87.5%, 86%, 82.5%, 80% indel guides
rationale: PTEN has the largest guide set and shows the sequence term working reasonably, but it is a systematic indictment of the accessibility gate: five guides editing above 80% sit in nominally closed chromatin and would all be filtered out. Recall loss here is not a rounding error, it is most of the usable guides.
An accessible target with a weak sequence score that failed entirely. Consistent with the sequence term dominating, but a single guide proves little.

issues: good outcome (65% indel) but fails the ATAC gate at 0.0775
would be a false negative of the Ito rule
rationale: DeepSpCas9 70.3 correctly anticipated a 65% indel, but the accessibility condition would have rejected this working guide. The sequence component is doing the useful work.
A clean concordant case where all three thresholds are met and the guide edited at 67%. Unreplicated, and its gate pass depends on an ATAC value only modestly above a noise-sensitive cutoff.

issues: strong sequence score with complete failure
rationale: A guide with genuinely strong sequence scores (seq_efficacy 0.73) produced zero editing, which the metric has no mechanism to anticipate. Both guides failing suggests a locus-level problem the score does not represent.

issues: top guide correctly identified (seq 0.75, ATAC 1.18, 85.2% indel)
but ATAC 0.0232 guide still achieved 70% indel
accessibility would reject a working guide
rationale: The metric correctly ranks the best RCOR1 guide first, which is the intended behavior. However a nominally closed guide also edited at 70%, so the accessibility term again costs recall without adding ranking value.
The sequence term ranks the two RUNX1 guides backwards, and accessibility is uniformly low so contributes nothing. Low trust in RUNX1 guide selection.

issues: better guide (53.5%) has lower ATAC (0.0232 vs 0.0775)
rationale: Sequence ordering is correct but accessibility is inverted between the two guides. Only one guide marginally clears 50% indel.
The far more accessible of the two guides failed completely while the less accessible one edited at 80.4%. The sequence term gets the ordering right; accessibility gets it exactly wrong.

issues: best guide (92% indel) fails the ATAC gate at 0.0775
rationale: Across four guides accessibility runs opposite to outcome: the least accessible guide edited best (92%) and the second-most accessible edited worst among the working guides (24.5%). The gate would recommend the wrong SELL guide.

issues: best guide (81% indel) fails CHOPCHOP gate at 0.20
rationale: The sequence term ranks SETDB1's guides approximately correctly, but the best guide would be rejected by the CHOPCHOP>=0.3 condition. Directionally usable, gate-unreliable.

issues: but the 0% guide sits at ATAC 2.04 - very open chromatin
accessibility would have recommended a completely failed guide
rationale: Sequence score cleanly separates the working guide from the failed one, which is the metric's core claim working. The failed guide's ATAC of 2.04 is another case where high accessibility accompanied zero editing.

issues: gate-passing guide gave only 29% indel (false positive)
rationale: Two guides pass the full Ito rule and return 29% and 70.5% - the rule cannot distinguish them, and one is a clear false positive. A third guide in open chromatin (ATAC 0.438) failed entirely.
An accessible target with a weak sequence score that produced almost no editing. Only the sequence term points the right way, and n=1.

issues: both guides edited well (67%, 73%) with low ATAC (0.0465, 0.031) and mediocre sequence scores
both would be rejected by the Ito gate
rationale: Two usable guides (67% and 73% indel) that both scored poorly on sequence and would be filtered out by accessibility. The metric would have discarded the whole gene.

issues: highest sequence score in the gene is the worst performer
rationale: The best-scoring SUV39H1 guide (seq_efficacy 0.76) edited at 1% while a lower-scoring guide reached 66%. This is a large, unexplained failure of the recommended ranking value at a locus where the metric expresses high confidence.

issues: very low scores (DeepSpCas9 21.4, CHOPCHOP 0.01) yet 28% indel
rationale: A guide the metric would rank near the bottom still produced 28% editing. Not a catastrophic error, but consistent with the score's systematic underprediction at the low end.

issues: best guide fails ATAC gate at 0.0775 while the failed guide has ATAC 0.232
rationale: Sequence score separates the two guides correctly and decisively (0.79 vs 0.38 for 82% vs 0% indel). Accessibility points the opposite way, which would flip the recommendation if it carried weight.
An accessible target that fell short of the efficiency bar. Single guide, no within-gene contrast, limited information.

issues: best guide correctly ranked first (seq 0.76 -> 71.3% indel)
but all 5 guides fail the ATAC gate (0.0155-0.0697)
accessibility contributes zero ranking information across the gene
rationale: The sequence term correctly identifies the best of five TET2 guides, which is genuinely useful. Accessibility is uniformly sub-threshold and would reject every guide including the working one.

issues: both guides edited moderately (65.5%, 40.5%) at extremely low ATAC (0.0155, 0.00775)
0.00775 is the single lowest ATAC bin - roughly one read count
rationale: A guide at the very bottom of the ATAC scale still achieved 40.5% indel and its partner reached 65.5%. Sequence ordering is correct; the accessibility premise fails outright at this locus.

issues: all 3 guides worked (97.4%, 77.4%, 59%) with ATAC above threshold
but sequence ordering is inverted (best indel has lowest DeepSpCas9)
rationale: TNF is one of the few genes where accessibility and outcome agree across all guides - three accessible targets, all editing well. Confidence is high for 'TNF guides will work' but the within-gene ranking is still inverted, so 'which TNF guide is best' remains unreliable.

issues: two guides at IDENTICAL ATAC 0.504 gave 60.7% and 19.5% indel
accessibility has no discriminating power at this locus
rationale: Two TOX guides share exactly the same accessibility value yet differ threefold in outcome, while a nearly closed guide performed comparably to the open ones. Accessibility is demonstrably not the operative variable here.

issues: 4 of 6 guides at 0-7% indel despite decent sequence scores
rationale: Most TOX2 guides fail regardless of score, including one with strong sequence metrics, while the guide with the lowest possible ATAC value edited at 56.5%. Both scored components are inverted or uninformative across this gene.

issues: 10 guides with near-constant ATAC (~0.0155-0.124) spanning 0-74.5% indel
best guide (74.5%) has the LOWEST ATAC (0.0155)
sequence scores tightly clustered (DeepSpCas9 59-72) with wildly different outcomes
rationale: TSC1 is the most informative negative case in the dataset: ten guides with nearly identical sequence scores (DeepSpCas9 59-72) produced outcomes from 0% to 74.5%, and accessibility ranks them backwards. Neither component explains the variance, which means most of the signal at this locus is something the metric does not measure.

issues: passes the FULL Ito rule (DeepSpCas9 67.0, CHOPCHOP 0.49, ATAC 0.136) yet 0% indel
rationale: This guide satisfies every condition of the validated Ito rule and produced literally zero editing. It is the most direct demonstration available that passing the gate does not guarantee function, and it is one of only 4 false positives inflating the gate's reported 0.862 precision.

issues: both guides 0% indel with mid-range sequence scores and ATAC 0.108 / 0.0697
one guide is above the ATAC threshold and still failed
rationale: Two guides with unremarkable but not disqualifying scores both produced zero editing, one of them in nominally accessible chromatin. No component anticipates this.

issues: rank inversion: CHOPCHOP 0.70 guide -> 11.5%, CHOPCHOP 0.35 guide -> 25.5%
both guides below the efficiency bar
ATAC 0.00775 (lowest bin) for the better guide
rationale: Both guides underperform and the metric orders them backwards. Nothing at this locus supports the score.

issues: DeepSpCas9 10.8 guide gave 27.5% - comparable to guides scoring 5x higher
rationale: Three guides with near-identical DeepSpCas9 scores (51-56) span 1.5% to 38.7% indel, so the score has no resolving power here, and the lowest-scoring guide performs mid-pack. All ZEB2 recommendations are effectively arbitrary.

issues: clear overprediction by the recommended score
rationale: A guide with strong sequence scores (seq_efficacy 0.65) that returned 12% editing. The recommended ranking value would have promoted a poor guide.

The single best-concordance case in the benchmark: highest sequence_efficacy in the dataset (0.861, DeepSpCas9 80.3, CHOPCHOP 0.92), ATAC 0.147, measured 83% indel, passing every threshold. Still unreplicated and off-target-unassessed, which is why this is 0.7 and not higher.

issues: ATAC 0.101 is ~1 read count above the 0.1 cutoff - gate pass is fragile
rationale: Strong concordance (seq_efficacy 0.74, DeepSpCas9 69.6, 73% indel). Its gate pass, however, hinges on an ATAC value of 0.101 against a 0.1 cutoff, a margin well inside the measurement's own quantization step.

issues: 72% indel but ATAC 0.0387 would reject it
rationale: DeepSpCas9 70.3 correctly predicted a well-performing guide (72% indel) that the accessibility gate would have discarded. Another instance of the sequence term carrying the prediction alone.

issues: passes full gate (DeepSpCas9 76.5, ATAC 0.112) but only 58% indel
rationale: A gate-passing guide with a high DeepSpCas9 score that returned a modest 58% indel - technically a true positive but well below what the score implies. ATAC 0.112 again sits close to the cutoff.
